description: A localization lead notices that product terms are being translated differently across help docs, app UI, and onboarding emails. They need to identify which terms have drifted and establish a single approved wording set for future work. All company names and products are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 35-year-old localization manager coordinating several freelance translators
user_profile.context: Support tickets are starting to reveal that inconsistent translated terms are confusing users in one major market
user_profile.communication_style: Precise and consistency-driven, wants wording differences surfaced with minimal ambiguity

fact_sheet.fact: The project to resolve translation inconsistencies is tracked in Jira under the ticket key LOC-734.
In October 2023, 18 support tickets were filed from the German market specifically mentioning confusion over the 'Insight Hub' feature.
Elara Vance is the Localization Manager at CogniSphere Inc., overseeing the SynapseFlow product.
The English source term 'Insight Hub' has been translated into German as 'Einblicks-Zentrale', 'Wissens-Hub', and 'Analysezentrum'.
CogniSphere Inc. uses LingoSync version 4.2 as its primary Translation Management System (TMS).
A new, centralized termbase for SynapseFlow will be established in LingoSync by November 30, 2023.
Klaus Richter is the primary freelance translator responsible for the German UI text of the SynapseFlow application.
Anja Schmidt is the freelance translator who handles localization for all German-language help documentation.
The translation 'Einblicks-Zentrale' is used in the SynapseFlow application UI, specifically in version 2.5.1 for desktop.
The translation 'Wissens-Hub' is used in the automated onboarding email sequence sent to new German users.
The translation 'Analysezentrum' is used in the online help documentation on the URL /help/insight-hub-overview.
The internal codename for the terminology consistency initiative is 'Project Unify'.
A user survey from Q3 2023 showed a 12% drop in satisfaction scores from German-speaking users regarding feature clarity.
The officially approved and finalized German translation for 'Insight Hub' is 'Einblicks-Zentrale'.
The approved termbase is accessible to all translators at the URL: https://cognisphere.lingosync.com/termbase/synapseflow.
Elara Vance's direct contact email for urgent queries is elara.vance@cognisphere.inc.
The deadline for updating all German help documentation with the approved terminology is December 15, 2023.
All freelance translators submit their work through the LingoSync portal; email submissions are not accepted.
The support ticket that first identified the inconsistency was #DE-98102, filed on October 5, 2023.
A mandatory training session on using the new termbase is scheduled for all German-language freelancers on November 28, 2023, at 10:00 AM CET.
The final list of 50 approved core terms must be signed off by David Chen, the Head of Product.
Another identified inconsistency is the feature 'Task Cascade', which has been translated as both 'Aufgabenkaskade' and 'Aufgaben-Reihenfolge'.
The approved German translation for 'Task Cascade' has been finalized as 'Aufgabenkaskade'.
All internal team communication regarding 'Project Unify' is centralized in the Slack channel #proj-unify.
The total budget allocated for the terminology audit and freelancer training for Project Unify is $4,500.
The average support ticket handling time for term-related confusion is 22 minutes, which is 8 minutes longer than the account average.
The source string files for the SynapseFlow UI are stored in a Git repository at git.cognisphere.net/synapseflow/frontend-strings.
